records.issue_text: admin-group.js.es6 addMembers action has no .catch/error handling if the addMembers promise rejects
records.rationale: The diff verifiably adds a new addMembers action whose call chain (controller action -> model.addMembers -> Discourse.ajax PUT) has no rejection handler anywhere, so a failed PUT to /admin/groups/:id/members.json would surface only through Ember's default unhandled-rejection path with no user feedback. This is accurate and specific to newly added code, but it is a robustness/error-handling concern rather than a demonstrable defect in the happy path, so it is not a bug.
records.stripped_text: admin-group.js.es6 addMembers action has no .catch/error handling if the addMembers promise rejects

records.issue_text: admin-group.js.es6 addMembers action never clears/resets the usernames field after adding members
records.rationale: The diff's addMembers action sets nothing after addMembers: `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get("usernames"))) { return; } this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` — usernames is never reset, so the input retains stale content. The code itself contains `// TODO: should clear the input`, confirming the defect exists (though acknowledged by the author).

records.issue_text: No rate limiting or upper bound on the user-controlled `limit` param in groups_controller.rb#members, allowing arbitrarily large DB queries (DoS)
records.rationale: The diff adds `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` in groups_controller.rb#members with no clamp; a client can pass limit=999999 to force a huge query (previously the limit only applied to automatic groups and defaulted to 200). This is a real, user-controllable unbounded query introduced by this change.

records.issue_text: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) which executes immediately, making the subsequent group.save a no-op, with no error handling if delete raises
records.rationale: The diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `if group.save ... else render_json_error(group)`. For a has_many :through association, delete removes the join record immediately, so the subsequent save is redundant, and if validations fail on save after the deletion already persisted, the error response would misreport state (deletion succeeded but error rendered). However, the member removal itself still functions correctly, so this is a code-quality/consistency concern rather than a verifiable functional defect. The error-handling point is vague (any unhandled exception would 500).
records.stripped_text: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) which executes immediately, making the subsequent group.save a no-op, with no error handling if delete raises
